subject: Initial sync: Reliability outline + action items
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintegrity.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Choudhary <aisha@fintegrity.com>, Fintegrity Legal <legal@fintegrity.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sync — reliability needs for Fintegrity

Ben / Priyom —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Wanted to capture the key reliability pain points we discussed and confirm what success looks like from our side so we can align on a PoC scope. I took notes below; please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of our environment and pain points:
- Product: real-time transaction decisioning (fraud scoring) across web + mobile.
- Traffic: steady 80–120 rps with 30% peaks during batch windows.
- Current stack: PyTorch models served on k8s; Redis for short-term KV cache; DB for audit logs.
- Incidents: two reliability events in last 12 months (Mar 2026, Aug 2026) where async queueing + model cold-start produced 3–6 minute latency spikes and missed SLAs for ~1.5 hours each. Root cause was scale-up slowdowns + cache churn.
- Pain: unpredictable tail latency, unclear fallback behavior when models are overloaded, and limited observability across multi-region traffic.

Success criteria (Fintegrity):
- Production SLO: 99.95% availability for decision latency under 300ms (90th percentile target 120ms).
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to lower-cost, lower-quality model (or cached response) with clear metrics and a testable rollback.
- Auditability: per-request logs and replay for compliance and fraud investigations.
- Cost control: measurable unit economics for token/embedding usage during spikes.

Asks from Fintegrity:
1) A short proposal for a 6-week PoC that proves: canary in us-west-2, fallback model behaviors, and prefix/KV caching to remove cold-starts.
2) SOC 2 evidence / security questionnaire for procurement.
3) Rough pricing for hosted vs. dedicated options for predictable peak capacity.

Happy to set a follow-up next week to lock the PoC scope — will loop in our Legal if needed.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure
Fintegrity

Subject: Re: Initial sync — reliability needs for Fintegrity

Samir —

Great notes, thanks for the recap. Confirming everything below and proposing concrete next steps so we can turn this into an executable mutual action plan.

Confirmed pain points (short):
- High tail latency during scale events driven by model cold-start and cache churn.
- Lack of deterministic fallback path when primary model degrades.
- Limited region failover testing and per-request observability for audit.

What Redwood will validate in the PoC:
- Model serving resilience: warm-up strategies, continuous batching, and KV cache to eliminate cold-starts.
- Graceful degradation: automatic routing to a compressed quantized variant (we generally recommend a 4–8x quantized fallback) or cached responses; documented expected quality delta with evaluation prompts.
- Multi-region failover: small canary in us-west-2 + cross-region failover test to us-east-1.
- SLO instrumentation: per-route latency metrics, error budgets and alerting hooks tied to your SLA.

Proposed PoC timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): security questionnaire, access & test account setup, initial data/traffic sample.
- Week 1–2: integration + baseline performance run (hosted sandbox).
- Week 3–4: canary deploy in us-west-2, run targeted failure injection (cache flush / model unavailability).
- Week 5: evaluate results, run rollback & fallback verification.
- Week 6: handoff & playbook + decision on hosted vs. dedicated.

Deliverables we will provide:
- SLO_template.xlsx (attached) with suggested alert windows and error-budget policies.
- Redwood_MVP_playbook.pdf (attached) — outlines fallback behaviors, quantization recommendations, and sample routing policies.
- Short eval report comparing primary vs fallback model quality on your sample prompts.

Open items for you (Fintegrity):
- Confirm sample traffic dataset and representative prompts (we asked for a 72-hour sample).
- SOC 2 / procurement timeline — do you expect Legal to need additional docs beyond the questionnaire?
- Decision on whether the PoC should use Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Hosted sandbox (faster iteration).

Next steps: can we do a 30-min scheduling call next Tue (Nov 24) to finalize scope and lock dates? Priyom will lead the technical onboarding and Grace will manage the SLO / playbook deliverable.

Thanks — I’ll also attach the SLO template and MVP playbook to this thread.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Initial sync — reliability needs for Fintegrity

Ben / Priyom —

Appreciate the detailed plan, that aligns with our expectations. A few clarifications and commitments from our side:
- We can provide a 72-hour traffic sample by Monday (Nov 23).
- Procurement: Legal will need SOC 2 Type II and a short data processing overview. They may ask about KMS integrations if we move to Private deployment.
- PoC preference: we prefer a hosted sandbox for the first 4 weeks for speed, but would like an option to toggle to a Dedicated pool for the canary if the baseline looks promising.
- Success gates: we agree on 99.95% availability and want a documented fallback-quality threshold (e.g., drop in precision < 5% on a representative fraud set).

Additional ask: can Redwood provide a short checklist for the failure-injection tests you propose? We want to make sure our SREs can run them safely.

We are available for the Tue (Nov 24) 30-min call — suggest 10:00 PT. Priyom, can you share an invite?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Fintegrity
